sections.h2: Where does Washington County keep its deed records?
sections.html:
At 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, mail to Box 1007 with the 27962 ZIP. The county page gives office hours of 8:30 to 5 on weekdays, phone (252) 793-2325 and fax (252) 793-6982.

Voters fill the register's seat for a four-year term, the county says. The office exists so that owners can put their interest in land on public notice, which in turn shields later buyers from unknown transactions and secret liens. It also issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses.

Washington County sits in the northeast of the state. By the county's description, US 64 cuts through it, Raleigh is about 120 miles west, Nags Head about 80 miles east and Greenville under 50 miles away. Plymouth, Roper and Creswell are its towns, and the Albemarle Sound shore is at Roper.

sections.h2: How old are the land records in Plymouth?
sections.html:
The oldest go back to 1799, the year Washington County was carved out of Tyrrell County. Marriage records start in 1851 and the licenses themselves in 1881.

The shelves hold old land grants, deeds, deeds of trust, maps, leases, agreements and powers of attorney. Anyone selling farmland or shoreline here should expect a long chain of title, and a title searcher will walk it back through those early books. A link on the county page opens deeds online.

North Carolina began statewide birth and death registration in 1913. Some earlier births appear in the county's files as delayed registrations filed by the person later. Older vital record requests should be in writing, with names and dates.

sections.h2: What steps come before a Washington County deed can be filed?
sections.html:
Two local checkpoints apply. First, every deed passes through the GIS (mapping) office to receive a parcel identifier number. Second, the county tax collector must certify that no delinquent taxes exist, or the deed itself must carry a statement from the closing lawyer promising to send any back taxes to the collector out of the closing funds. The statement route is the usual one.

  • Name the person who prepared the deed on page one.
  • Choose letter or legal size paper, with a three-inch blank band across the top of the first page and quarter-inch margins on the remaining edges.
  • Print in black on white, nothing smaller than nine point, on one side only.
  • Label the type of instrument at the top of page one.

A paper that misses those standards is still accepted, but the register adds a $25 non-standard charge to the normal fee. The county also mentions that cancellations and satisfactions can be sent through Simplifile.

sections.h2: What does it cost to file in Washington County?
sections.html:
The county prints the uniform schedule from G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at twenty-six dollars, which covers fifteen pages, with four dollars for each page beyond. A deed of trust starts at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five pages and takes the same four-dollar surcharge per added page.

Maps are routed through GIS for a parcel number and through the county review officer for approval, unless the map carries one of three stock statements: no new street, an existing building or natural feature, or a control survey.

sections.h2: Who covers the stamp tax on a Plymouth-area sale?
sections.html:
The person transferring the property. The register collects it before the deed goes on record, at one dollar per $500 or fraction of the price or value.

The county reproduces the same rate on its page, and G.S. 105-228.30 divides the money between county and state. The settlement statement will show the stamp, so no one has to calculate it in advance. If a deed has no ordinary sale price, ask the register how the stamp applies before you bring it in.

sections.h2: Does the Washington County office file contracts for deed?
sections.html:
It files any instrument touching land, and seller financing is a common case. Under Chapter 47H, a contract for deed on a one to four family home must be written, signed and acknowledged, and the seller has five business days to record the contract or a memorandum of it.

The buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day. If the seller later seeks forfeiture, the written default notice must give a cure date at least thirty days after service.

Other things a Washington County seller may bring to the counter:

  • A power of attorney, if someone signs the deed for the owner.
  • A map or plat in the 18 by 24 format, after GIS review.
  • A lease or agreement, both listed among the county's record types.

Because the preparer must be named on page one, line up whoever drafts the deed before you go.

sections.h2: What else brings Plymouth residents to the register?
sections.html:
Marriage licenses are a regular errand. Any North Carolina register will issue one, and the ceremony can be held in any county, but the signed license must come back to the county that sold it. Each applicant needs a driver's license and a Social Security card, or a W-2, pay stub, insurance card or Social Security printout as proof of the number. Blood tests and physicals are no longer required.

Applicants aged 16 to 17 bring a certified birth certificate, and anyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's consent. Those under 16 must call the office first.

Vital record copies follow a tight rule: certified ones go only to the applicant or immediate family, and in-person requests need identification. The same counter that handles those errands is the one that files your deed, so allow time on busy days.

sections.h2: Why does filing order matter in Washington County?
sections.html:
Because the earliest registration wins. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until registered in the county where the land lies.

  • For a deed naming more than twenty parties, call (252) 793-2325 first.
  • Ask the tax collector about open bills, since the deed needs the certification or the lawyer's statement.
  • Check whether an old loan still lacks a recorded satisfaction.

Shoreline and farm parcels often carry surveys, and any plat that comes with the sale follows the map rules above.

sections.h2: Can a Washington County house with title or tax problems still sell?
sections.html:
Yes. A closing lawyer clears unpaid taxes and liens from the price, and a buyer can take the house in its present condition. Searching the register's index is the first move for any title searcher.

To weigh a cash offer on a Washington County house against a listing, you can request a written offer on this site.

faqs.q: Does Washington County charge to record a satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. The county lists cancellations and certificates of satisfaction as free, and the non-standard document fee never applies to a cancellation.

faqs.q: Is a parcel number needed before a Washington County deed is filed?
faqs.a: Yes. The county sends every deed to GIS first so a parcel identifier number can be assigned.

faqs.q: What does a certified birth, death or marriage copy cost in Washington County?
faqs.a: The county prints ten dollars for certified and twenty-five cents for uncertified. Certified copies go only to the applicant or immediate family, and faxed requests are refused.

faqs.q: How long does a Washington County marriage license last?
faqs.a: Sixty days, at a cost of sixty dollars. The county asks applicants to arrive before 4:30 p.m. because the visit takes fifteen to twenty minutes.

faqs.q: Whom do I phone about filing a Washington County deed?
faqs.a: The register of deeds at (252) 793-2325. The office is at 120 Adams Street in Plymouth, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5.
